seo.title: AI Agent Workspace for Small Business Teams | Floatboat
seo.description: An AI agent workspace for small businesses to prepare customer work, coordinate operations, organize recurring files, and keep important actions under human control.

hero.title: AI Agent Workspace for Small Business
hero.description: Connect customer requests, operating files, staff handoffs, recurring reviews, and owner decisions in a workspace that produces editable work instead of another queue to manage.

burdens.title: Small teams lose time at every handoff
burdens.description: Customer, operations, finance, and scheduling systems each hold part of the truth, while staff still reconstruct the complete job by hand.

items.label: Intake
items.title: A customer request arrives incomplete
items.description: Important scope, timing, price, inventory, or service details must be recovered before anyone can respond accurately.

items.label: Handoff
items.title: The next person cannot see the whole job
items.description: Messages, files, promises, and changes travel through separate tools, leaving staff to ask the same questions again.

items.label: Routine
items.title: Recurring administration still starts manually
items.description: Weekly updates, vendor checks, customer follow-ups, and reporting depend on someone remembering the next step.

items.label: Control
items.title: Automation can move faster than policy
items.description: A drafted quote or message is useful, but sending it without the right price, permission, or owner review creates risk.

workflows.title: Prepare the work that crosses roles and tools
workflows.description: These examples organize existing business information and stop before customer, financial, or policy commitments are made.

items.title: Turn a customer request into a work packet
items.job: Combine the incoming request with approved service details, customer history, and missing questions.
items.output: A response draft, quote worksheet, assumptions, and delivery checklist.
items.boundary: Staff approve price, availability, terms, recipient, and any customer commitment.

items.title: Coordinate an operational handoff
items.job: Bring files, decisions, responsibilities, deadlines, and unresolved issues into one handoff brief.
items.output: A handoff brief, file index, action register, and open-issue list.
items.boundary: Managers confirm responsibilities, access, deadlines, and changes to the operating plan.

items.title: Prepare a weekly owner review
items.job: Summarize approved customer, operational, cash, staffing, and vendor updates around decisions that need attention.
items.output: A concise operating brief with source links, exceptions, and decision prompts.
items.boundary: The business owner validates figures and decides priorities, spending, staffing, and external action.

faq.title: Small business AI workspace questions
faq.description: A small business needs useful automation that respects its systems of record, staff permissions, customer promises, and owner approval.

items.question: Does Floatboat replace our CRM, accounting, or project system?
items.answer: No. Those systems remain authoritative. Floatboat helps prepare cross-system work from the files and information your team is permitted to use.

items.question: Can it quote a customer automatically?
items.answer: It can prepare a quote worksheet from approved pricing and scope information, but an authorized person should confirm price, availability, terms, and recipient before sending.

items.question: Can different staff members use the same workflow?
items.answer: A proven method can be shared when the team has appropriate access, ownership, and approval rules. Shared does not mean every person should see every file.

items.question: How do we handle customer and employee information?
items.answer: Follow applicable policy and obligations, minimize the data used, scope access by role, and review how each selected model and connector processes it.

items.question: Can it update external business systems?
items.answer: That depends on the available integration and permissions. Treat writes, sends, financial changes, and irreversible actions as separate approval points.

items.question: What should a small business automate first?
items.answer: Start with a repeated preparation task such as an intake packet or weekly owner brief, not a high-risk decision or unattended external action.

items.question: How is this different from a solopreneur workflow?
items.answer: A small business page emphasizes handoffs, role-based access, shared review, and continuity between people; the solopreneur page emphasizes one person switching roles.

finalCta.title: Connect the work between your business systems
finalCta.description: Choose one customer or operating process with known inputs and a responsible reviewer. Improve the handoff before expanding the automation.
